rationale: The resumed ascent from Abdedom’s house follows the earlier interruption in which the ark stayed three months in the house named Abeddara and God blessed Abeddaram. All three source forms remain distinct within the consecutive ark narrative.
The song links the covenant with Abraham and God’s oath to Isaac; God’s promise to Isaac in Genesis explicitly establishes the oath sworn to Abraham and promises the land to Isaac and his seed.

David contrasts his cedar house with the ark’s temporary shelter before Nathan in both accounts; Chronicles says beneath skins, while Samuel calls it the tent and adds possession on every side away from surrounding enemies.

Both prayers invoke the Lord Almighty, God of Israel, in connection with His word about David’s house; Chronicles asks that the house stand upright, while Samuel asks confirmation of the word and magnification of God’s name.

David consecrates silver and gold taken from the nations; the later treasury notice explicitly includes holy things consecrated by David and gifts taken from wars and spoils for the building of God’s house. It does not identify every item in this campaign list individually.

Both follow the messengers’ shaming with Ammon hiring Syrian aid. Chronicles specifies a thousand talents and chariots and horsemen from its named regions; Samuel lists twenty thousand foot soldiers and additional numbered groups of men, with different regional wording.
